6213.t: Unknown, perhaps Pre-Greek. Probably cognate, ancestor, or descendant of Latin calx (“limestone, chalk”).

6214.t: Likely related to χαῦνος (khaûnos, “porous, loose-grained”) (via an earlier form χάος (kháos) < *χάϝος (*kháwos)), with original meaning "hole, empty space, yawning opening"; from this spring the traditional connections with χάσκω (kháskō, “to gape,…

6256.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂mélǵti, from *h₂melǵ- (“to milk”). Cognates include Latin mulgeō, Old English meolc (English milk), Gothic 𐌼𐌹𐌻𐌿𐌺𐍃 (miluks), and Albanian mjel.

6207.t: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰerH- (“bowel”), but the exact formation is unclear.

6203.t: Of unclear origin. Traditionally connected with χηραμός (khērămós, “hole, hollow”), χήμη (khḗmē, “yawning, gaping”), and χάσκω (kháskō, “to yawn, gape”), but the supposed unifying connections are obscure.

6221.t: If it dissimilated from *ψυθυρ-, it may belong to ψύθος (psúthos, “lie, untruth”). On the other hand, it can be compared to ψίζομαι (psízomai, “to weep”).

6242.t: From an uncertain source apparently shared with Sanskrit अक्तु (aktú, “beam, ray”), perhaps: * Proto-Indo-European *h₂ekt- (“beam”), from an unidentified root; * Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp point”), which would exclude the Sanskrit; *…

6223.t: ἀ- (a-, “not”, alpha privativum) + βουλή (boulḗ, “will, determination, decision”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, abstract-noun-forming suffix)

6211.t: Apparently from a Proto-Indo-European *gʰreh₁-, *ǵʰreh₁- (“to desire, need”), with relation to other roots uncertain.

6215.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʰumə, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéwmn̥, from *ǵʰew- (“to pour”), whence χέω (khéō).

6266.t: ἀνα- (ana-) + σκάπτω (skáptō) The present tense system includes a T progressive aspect marker.

6253.t: As if from *ἄμνητος (ámnētos) ("forgetful") + -ία (-íā), from ἀ- (a-) + μιμνήσκω (mimnḗskō) + -τος (-tos).

6228.t: From ἀδάμας, ἀ˘δαμαντ- (adámās, ădămănt-, “diamond; steel”) + -ινος (-ĭnos, suffix).

6238.t: From ἀ- (ă-, not; without) + κλέω (kléō, “to make famous”) + -ής (-ḗs, adjective suffix).

6298.t: From ἀπο- (apo-) + the root -η(ν)- (-ē(n)-) found in πρανής (prānḗs, “prone”) and ἐνηής (enēḗs, “gentle, amiable”).

6269.t: From ἀνα- (ănă-, “up”) + τρέχω (trékhō, “to run, run over”).

6294.t: From ἀ- (a-, “a-, un-”) + παραιτέομαι (păraitéomai, “to beg, entreat”) + -τος (-tos).
